newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortage insurance bill introduced.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortage insurance bill introduced.

text.p: Homebuyers would have to be informed about their right to cancel mortgage insurance policies after they have paid off 20 percent of the original loan value under a bill introduced on Thursday by Sen. Alfonse D'Amato, R-New York, and Rep. James Hansen, R-Utah.
They said many homebuyers do not know they do not need mortgage insurance after they have paid 20 percent of the loan and continue to pay premiums.
"Consumers are unkowingly paying anywhere from $240 to $1,200 a month for absolutely no reason," D'Amato said.
